source: MAFF / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), Royal Government of Cambodia — ខ្សែសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំស្វាយចន្ទីនៅកម្ពុជា (Cashew Value Chain Study in Cambodia), field survey report (250 household respondents across major cashew-growing provinces), 2017, 57pp
text:
Overview of a 2017 field-survey study on the cashew (ស្វាយចន្ទី, Anacardium occidentale) value chain in Cambodia, conducted under MAFF's Boosting Food Production Program (PMO) and covering roughly 250 farming households across the major cashew-growing provinces.

The study's stated objectives were: (1) to identify the problems facing actors along the cashew value chain; (2) to find solutions for better market linkages among value-chain actors; and (3) to determine the needs of trading partners along the value chain, in order to help find sustainable solutions for growers.

Cashew is treated in the report as a strategic diversification crop, valuable especially for farmers on marginal or degraded land (including former conflict-affected and sandy/poor-soil areas) where other crops perform poorly, because cashew tolerates low-input conditions, helps prevent land erosion, and provides income diversification.

National cashew planting area grew substantially in the years before this study: from about 193,781 hectares in 2012 to about 238,780 hectares in 2016 (roughly a 23% increase over four years), based on MAFF annual reports cited in the source.

The survey covered major cashew provinces including Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Kratie, and others, and also examined the downstream link to Vietnam, which the report identifies as the dominant export market for Cambodia's raw cashew nut.
caveat: Some specific figures in this source (percentages, price points, yield ranges) were transcribed from a scanned document at a resolution where certain digits were hard to confirm with full pixel-level certainty. Figures are reported as best-effort readings of the source; anyone using exact numbers for decisions should verify against the original report where possible.
